{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
file_path = "/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/sales.csv"
data = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
if data['revenue'].str.contains(',', na=False).any():
    data['revenue_clean'] = data['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)
else:
    data['revenue_clean'] = data['revenue'].astype(float)

# Remove QA orders (revenue == 999999.99) and refunded orders
qa_mask = (data['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99)
refunded_mask = (data['status'] == 'refunded')
completed_mask = (data['status'] == 'completed')

filtered_data = data[completed_mask & ~qa_mask]

# Group by channel and compute average revenue
avg_revenue_by_channel = filtered_data.groupby('channel')['revenue_clean'].mean()

# Also compute total revenue and count for transparency
summary = filtered_data.groupby('channel').agg(
    avg_revenue=('revenue_clean', 'mean'),
    total_revenue=('revenue_clean', 'sum'),
    count=('revenue_clean', 'count')
)

# Check if the email channel is biased toward high-value customers
segment_by_channel = filtered_data.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)

# Compute difference in average revenue
email_avg = avg_revenue_by_channel['email']
paid_search_avg = avg_revenue_by_channel['paid_search']
difference = email_avg - paid_search_avg

# Print all results
print("Summary by channel:")
print(summary)

print("\nCustomer segment distribution by channel:")
print(segment_by_channel)

print(f"\nAverage revenue (email): {email_avg:.2f} USD")
print(f"Average revenue (paid_search): {paid_search_avg:.2f} USD")
print(f"Difference (email - paid_search): {difference:.2f} USD")"}
